title: Inverse image, tensor product and extension by zero preserve $D^b_c(-,\mathcal O_E)$
statement:
Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite and all schemes Noetherian.

1. For $f\colon X\to Y$ and $K\in\Dbc(Y,\cO_E)$, $f^*K\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$.
2. For $K,M\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$, $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\cO_{E,X}}M\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$ (no completion is
   needed).
3. For a locally closed immersion $a=i\circ u\colon S\hookrightarrow\overline S\hookrightarrow X$
   and $L\in\Dbc(S,\cO_E)$, $a_!L=i_*u_!L\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$.
4. For $a$ as in (3), $L\in D(S_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)$ and $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)$,
   $(a_!L)\otimes^{\mathbf L}M\simeq a_!(L\otimes^{\mathbf L}a^*M)$.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_E$, $R_T=\mathcal O_{E,T}$. Use bounded cohomology with finite constant scalar-model constructibility [sk-def-sfb-constructible]; no completeness is imposed.

For (1), [lem-sfb-pullback-constant-model-constructible] preserves constructible sheaves (quasi-compact by hypothesis and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]). Cartesian pullback is exact, so its derived functor is termwise [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], hence $H^q(f^*K)=f^*H^q(K)$ with unchanged bounds.

For (3), [lem-sfb-scalar-model-immersion-extension] preserves constructible sheaves under $u_!$ and $i_*$. Their exactness implies $H^q(i_*u_!L)=i_*u_!H^q(L)$ with the same bounds; their derived functors are termwise. Hence $a_!L\in\Dbc(X,A)$.

For constructible sheaves $F,G$, intersect adapted strata [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-stratification-intersection], then their trivializing covers by site base change and composition. Pullback preserves the scalar models. Monoidal derived pullback identifies the restricted tensor with $(R_V\otimes_A P)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_V}(R_V\otimes_A Q)$. Here $A$ is a DVR and $A_V\to R_V$ is flat. The cyclic resolutions [lem-sfb-flat-scalar-cyclic-resolution] compute the torsion factors; [lem-sfb-flat-dvr-scalar-tensor] supplies finite scalar cohomology models in degrees $-1,0$. Exact restrictions and stratum-and-cover detection give the global vanishing; these models certify constructibility.

Integral scalar-model sheaves are closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions by [lem-sfb-integral-constant-model-heart-closure]; the weak-Serre cohomology theorem makes their bounded derived subcategory triangulated. Derived tensor is exact in both variables. Apply [lem-sfb-bounded-bifunctor-devissage] to the sheaf case of step 4. This proves (2) for bounded constructible $K,M$, using ambient tensors throughout.

For (4), [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] gives the unbounded open projection formula for $u$ and ring $R_{\overline S}$ (identity base-change square). Cartesian coefficients identify the restricted rings. [lem-weil-proetale-closed-tensor-projection] gives the closed formula for $i$; its complementary open is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets] ($|X|$ is Noetherian).

Apply the closed formula to $N=u_!L$, then the open formula inside $\overline S$. This gives $$(i_*u_!L)\otimes^{\mathbf L}M\simeq i_*(u_!L\otimes^{\mathbf L}i^*M)\simeq i_*u_!(L\otimes^{\mathbf L}u^*i^*M).$$ Composition of inverse images gives $u^*i^*=a^*$, proving (4) naturally in $L,M$. The extension by zero of step 6 is $u_!$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]: both are left adjoint to restriction under $u^{-1}R_{\overline S}=R_S$ [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. As $i_*,u_!,i^*$ are exact, $Ri_*=i_*$, $Li^*=i^*$ termwise [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories].

Only clause (1), flatness of constant-to-completed coefficients, is used; derived completeness is not imposed.

Turns the verified heart closure into a triangulated bounded cohomology subcategory.
Supplies exactness in both variables of uncompleted derived tensor.
Its gamma is the projection formula for an arbitrary ring sheaf and arbitrary unbounded inputs; the identity square supplies the open part of (4).
Supplies the closed part of (4) for arbitrary unbounded inputs with a quasi-compact complementary open.
Makes the complementary opens quasi-compact, with no finite-type-over-a-field assumption.
Identifies the composite inverse image with successive inverse images in the final formula.
